picks.title: The inside story behind OpenAI's million-dollar math proof
picks.excerpt: AI's solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, and the details of how it happened, preview a chaotic future for mathematics.
picks.rationale: Math slot: the first account in our feed of the AI-produced Navier-Stokes (Millennium Prize) result. It is a different problem from the 10-17 SciAm encryption card, and the biggest AI-for-science story in the pool.

picks.title: New superconducting chip aims to help tame fusion plasma
picks.excerpt: Researchers fed fusion data to a new neuromorphic superconducting chip to test whether it can spot signs that superhot plasma is about to go unstable.
picks.rationale: Physics/hardware slot: a neuromorphic superconducting chip was tested on real fusion data to flag plasma instabilities. This is new hardware meeting a hard physics problem.

picks.title: Using AI agents to run quantum simulations
picks.excerpt: Researchers developed a multi-agent AI system that converts plain-language research questions into executed, checked and reproducible quantum simulations across several specialist software packages.
picks.rationale: Research-method slot: an academic multi-agent system turns plain-language questions into checked, reproducible quantum simulations across specialist codes. It is a different system from Haiqu's commercial AgenticOS (10-08).

picks.title: Researchers find a way to reduce AI chatbots' reinforcement of delusions
picks.excerpt: Georgia Tech researchers ran 1,280 simulated conversations with eight AI models; anti-sycophancy instructions cut affirmation of delusional beliefs by 73.8%, rising to 77% with a self-reflection step (ACM AI Letters).
picks.rationale: AI-behavior slot: a quantified result (1,280 simulated conversations, 8 models) showing that anti-sycophancy prompts cut affirmation of delusions by about 74-77%. It is a model-behavior study, not a clinical one.

picks.title: AI listens to bee buzzes to monitor activity without lethal traps
picks.excerpt: UMass Amherst researchers built two deep learning models that analyse field audio to measure bee activity and tell honeybees from bumblebees with 93-97% accuracy, offering an alternative to lethal pan traps.
picks.rationale: Ecology slot: audio deep learning tells honeybees from bumblebees with 93-97% accuracy, replacing lethal pan traps. It is unrelated to the 09-28 bee-repellent chemistry card.
